atoms.text: Rivers flow over areas of both hard rock and soft rock.
Soft rock erodes quicker, which creates a dip in the river.
Over time, the dip gets bigger as the river continues flowing over the edge of the hard rock and eroding the soft rock below. This is now known as a waterfall.
Eventually, the overhanging hard rock will collapse and fall into the pool below. Due to this, all waterfalls are gradually moving upstream.
